paper.title: Recombination Rate and Selection Strength in HIV Intra-patient Evolution
paper.citation: Neher RA, Leitner T. Recombination rate and selection strength in HIV intra-patient evolution. PLoS Comput Biol 6(1):e1000660 (2010).

inputs.name: set1_clinical_data.txt (LANL special interest set 1, visit numbers to months)
set1_Shriner.fasta (212 Shriner 2004 clones, used only in the hypothesis tests)
muscle3.6_src.tar.gz (MUSCLE 3.6, public domain, built from source)

items.label: Fig. 1, how recombination makes the missing haplotype

cause.summary: A drawing of two sites and four haplotypes. It shows no data.

assumptions.what: Seven distance bins of 76.6 bp, from 0 to 536 bp. The paper does not give the bins; the published points sit at 38, 114, 190, 267, 343, 420 and 496 bp.
assumptions.sensitivity: Six or eight bins move each point by up to 0.02, below the error bars of the outer bins.

assumptions.what: Distance is the number of alignment columns between the two sites.
assumptions.sensitivity: Counting only ungapped consensus columns shortens the longest distances by about 10 percent and moves no point by more than 0.01.

cause.summary: The recombinant curve matches the published one to 300 bp and then stays 0.03 to 0.06 low, and the other-haplotype curve runs 0.02 to 0.08 high. Both follow from an alignment and a sequence set that are not exactly the paper's.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The distance bins are wrong.
hypotheses.test: Six, seven and eight bins over 0 to 536 bp: the top bin stays between 0.288 and 0.292 and the other-haplotype rise stays at 0.055.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The alignment differs. MUSCLE 3.6 as its 2005 ia32 binary and as a build of its own source give different alignments.
hypotheses.test: Both run end to end: 9,295 against 9,621 qualifying pairs, c2 5.65e-05 against 4.06e-05 and rho 1.25e-05 against 9.79e-06.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The paper used the whole LANL special interest set 1, which holds 212 Shriner 2004 sequences for patients 2, 3, 7, 8 and 9 outside its accession list.
hypotheses.test: Added them and reran: 14,366 pairs, <M pA pB> 1.33 and rho 6.4e-06, further from the paper.

items.label: Fig. 2B, missing haplotype against distance times time, with the fit

assumptions.what: Bins of 8,000 bp x generations. The paper does not give them; the published points sit at 4,000, 12,000, 20,000 and so on.
assumptions.sensitivity: At 6,000 the fit gives c2 = 3.6e-05 and rho = 8.9e-06; at 10,000, c2 = 4.2e-05 and rho = 1.0e-05.

assumptions.what: The squared residuals are weighted by the relative uncertainty 1 / sqrt(counts) rather than by the error bar p / sqrt(counts).
assumptions.sensitivity: Weighting by the error bar gives c0 = 0.075, c1 = 0.240, c2 = 7.3e-05 and rho = 1.6e-05, and a bootstrap spread ten times the paper's.

cause.summary: Seven of the nine points sit inside the published error bars; two (28,000 and 44,000 bp x generations) are 0.04 and 0.06 low. The bins hold 100 to 1,000 pairs, so single pairs moving in or out of the biallelic and gapless set shift them.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The bin width is wrong.
hypotheses.test: 6,000 and 10,000 bp x generations: c2 3.6e-05 and 4.2e-05, rho 8.9e-06 and 1.0e-05.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The alignment differs.
hypotheses.test: The 2005 MUSCLE binary moves the two missing points from 0.256 to 0.264 and from 0.294 to 0.304, still short of the published 0.299 and 0.354.

items.label: Fig. 2B legend: c0, c1 and c2 of the fit

assumptions.what: The fit's three constants are compared with the spread of the same fit over the 500 resamples of the patients (c0 +-0.025, c1 +-0.093, c2 +-1.7e-05), the uncertainty the paper itself quotes for the rate.
assumptions.sensitivity: At printed precision c1 still comes back and c0 and c2 miss by 0.006 and 0.33e-05.

assumptions.what: The fit runs on bins of 8,000 bp x generations, read from the published Figure 2B; the paper does not give them.
assumptions.sensitivity: At 6,000 and 10,000 the rate is 8.9e-06 and 1.0e-05 against 9.8e-06.

items.label: Methods: <M pA pB> ~ 0.93 measured in the data

cause.summary: Ours is 1.19 against the paper's 0.93. This one number sets the rate through rho = c1 c2 / (<M pA pB> - c0): with the paper's 0.93 our fit gives 1.3e-05 against its 1.4e-05.

hypotheses.hypothesis: It uses another sample size or another pair of alleles.
hypotheses.test: All four combinations of M at t_i or t_i+1 with the minor alleles or the missing haplotype's alleles, and min(M): 1.04, 1.19, 1.35, 1.41 and 1.60. None reaches 0.93.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The sequence set differs.
hypotheses.test: Adding the 212 Shriner 2004 clones raises it to 1.33.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The alignment differs.
hypotheses.test: The 2005 MUSCLE binary gives 1.20.

items.label: Abstract and Eq. 3: rho = 1.4 +- 0.6 x 10^-5 per site and generation

cause.summary: rho = 9.8e-06 against 1.4e-05, inside the paper's own one standard deviation, which is the tolerance the paper gives the number. The gap follows from <M pA pB>: with the paper's 0.93 our fit gives 1.3e-05.

hypotheses.hypothesis: <M pA pB> uses another convention.
hypotheses.test: Five conventions, 1.04 to 1.60; none reaches 0.93. With the paper's 0.93 our fit gives rho 1.3e-05.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The alignment differs.
hypotheses.test: The 2005 MUSCLE binary gives rho 1.25e-05 and a bootstrap standard deviation of 0.56e-05, both close to the paper's 1.4e-05 and 0.6e-05. It moves toward the paper but does not close the gap.

assumptions.what: The fit runs on bins of 8,000 bp x generations, read from the published Figure 2B; the paper does not give them.
assumptions.sensitivity: At 6,000 and 10,000 the rate is 8.9e-06 and 1.0e-05 against 9.8e-06.

assumptions.what: The squared residuals are weighted by the relative uncertainty 1/sqrt(counts) rather than by the error bar p/sqrt(counts).
assumptions.sensitivity: Weighting by the error bar gives 1.6e-05 and a bootstrap spread ten times the paper's.

items.label: Fig. 3, the printed mean, median and standard deviation of the bootstrap

assumptions.what: The bootstrap seed. The paper gives none; we use numpy's default_rng(0) and 500 resamples of the 11 patients.
assumptions.sensitivity: Seeds 1 to 5 move the mean by less than 4 percent and the standard deviation by less than 8 percent.

cause.summary: Our bootstrap sits at mean 0.92e-05, median 0.83e-05 and standard deviation 0.39e-05, against 1.51, 1.38 and 0.55. The distribution has the paper's shape and spread but a lower centre, which follows from rho itself.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The seed matters.
hypotheses.test: Seeds 0 to 5: the mean stays between 9.13e-06 and 9.41e-06, the standard deviation between 3.38e-06 and 4.06e-06.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The alignment differs.
hypotheses.test: The 2005 MUSCLE binary gives mean 1.17e-05, median 1.07e-05 and standard deviation 0.56e-05, against the paper's 1.51, 1.38 and 0.55. It moves toward the paper but does not close the gap.

items.label: Fig. 3, bootstrap distribution of the recombination rate

assumptions.what: 30 histogram bins from 0 to 30 x 10^-6 and a count axis to 160, read from the published panel's bars and ticks.
assumptions.sensitivity: 20 bins instead of 30 moves the score from 0.327 to 0.294.

cause.summary: On the published axes our histogram sits about 0.5e-05 to the left of the published one: its peak is at 9 to 10 x 10^-6 where the published peak is at 13 to 15. A wrong-input control (a flat distribution) now scores better than our histogram, so the panel differs.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The bin count or the axes are wrong.
hypotheses.test: The axes are read from the published panel (0 to 30 x 10^-6, 0 to 160 counts) and 20 bins instead of 30 moves the score by 0.03.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The distribution itself is shifted, as its printed statistics are.
hypotheses.test: The 2005 MUSCLE alignment moves the mean from 0.92e-05 to 1.17e-05 and the median to 1.07e-05.

assumptions.what: A site is synonymous or non-synonymous by putting its two alleles into the consensus codon of the earlier sample. The paper does not say which codon background it used.
assumptions.sensitivity: Using each sequence's own codon changes the class of under 2 percent of the observations.

cause.summary: 15 of the 18 readable points of the three curves match within two standard errors. The three misses are each under 0.03 of probability, at the steepest part of the curves. The curves are normalized, so they hide the difference in the counts behind them, which the inset shows.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The synonymous and non-synonymous classes use another codon background.
hypotheses.test: The consensus of the later sample instead of the earlier one: 2,533 against 2,541 non-synonymous observations and the same share above 0.002 per generation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The three misses are sampling noise.
hypotheses.test: Each is under 0.03 of probability and inside three standard errors of a share on our counts.

items.label: Fig. 4 inset, the observation counts per bin

assumptions.what: The inset's 21 bins from 0 to 0.011 per generation and its log axis, read from the published panel; a class drawn under a taller one cannot be read and is left out.
assumptions.sensitivity: The three classes are read in 15, 10 and 6 of the 21 bins.

cause.summary: Our run has fewer observations than the paper's, and the gap grows with the filtering: the non-synonymous counts match in 9 of 15 readable bins, the synonymous in 4 of 10 (ours about half the paper's), and the synonymous without hitch-hiking in none of 6. The paper's first bin alone holds about 1,310 of that class where our whole filtered set holds 195.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Our hitch-hiking filter removes far more than the paper's.
hypotheses.test: 195 of 1,060 synonymous observations survive it here (18 percent); the published inset keeps about 1,850 of its synonymous observations. Windows of 50, 100, 150 and 200 bp leave 392, 195, 123 and 71, so no window of the stated form keeps that many.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The counts differ because the sequence set differs.
hypotheses.test: Adding the 212 Shriner 2004 clones raises the synonymous count, but it also moves the recombination rate away from the paper.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The classification differs.
hypotheses.test: The consensus of the later sample changes 8 of 3,601 observations.

items.label: Results: 15% of non-synonymous polymorphisms change faster than 0.002 per generation

cause.summary: Four of the five counted fields come back: more fast non-synonymous than synonymous polymorphisms, the synonymous share above 0.002 per generation, the fastest non-synonymous change (0.011 against 0.01) and the selection coefficient of the top sixth (0.0083 against 0.008). Two of our 195 synonymous observations without hitch-hiking lie beyond 0.003 per generation, where the paper reports none. The paper's own Figure 4 puts its non-synonymous share above 0.002 at 17.2 percent where its text says about 15; ours is 15.9, between the two, so that field is excepted.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The hitch-hiking filter is read wrongly (100 bp, faster than 0.002 per generation).
hypotheses.test: Windows of 50, 100, 150 and 200 bp leave 392, 195, 123 and 71 observations with fastest rates 0.0052, 0.0041, 0.0022 and 0.0020. Only 150 bp or more brings the tail below 0.003, and the paper states 100 bp.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Our filtered set is too small for its tail to be comparable.
hypotheses.test: 195 observations here against about 1,850 in the published inset; two of ours lie beyond 0.003.

fields.name: more fast non-synonymous than fast synonymous polymorphisms
share of synonymous faster than 0.002 per generation
share of synonymous without hitch-hiking beyond 0.003 per generation
selection coefficient of the top 15% (s >= 4 dp/dt)

evidence: The text says about 15 percent; the paper's own Figure 4 puts the non-synonymous curve at 0.828 at 0.002 per generation, which is 17.2 percent. Ours, 15.9 percent, lies between the two.

items.label: Results: the two Kolmogorov-Smirnov p values

cause.summary: The first p value comes back (7.6e-14, below 1e-13) and the Kolmogorov-Smirnov D matches at 0.14. The second is 3.6e-21 against the paper's bound of 1e-25, because our synonymous set without hitch-hiking holds 195 observations and D is 0.36, where the published inset holds about 1,850.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Our filtered set is too small to reach 1e-25.
hypotheses.test: 195 observations at D = 0.36 give 3.6e-21. The published inset of Figure 4 holds about 1,850 observations of that class, nine times ours.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The filter removes too much.
hypotheses.test: A 50 bp window leaves 392 observations and gives 1.6e-24, still above 1e-25; a 150 bp window leaves 123 and gives 4.8e-22.

fields.name: p, non-synonymous vs synonymous without hitch-hiking (< 1e-25)

items.label: Results: the other-haplotype curve does not rise with distance

cause.summary: Our other-haplotype curve is far flatter than the recombinant curve, as the paper says, but it rises by 0.054 over 500 bp with a standard error of 0.017, so it is not consistent with no distance dependence. The published curve falls by 0.041 over the same range.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The bins are wrong.
hypotheses.test: Six, seven and eight bins: the rise stays at 0.055.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The alignment differs; this curve counts nucleotides at t_i+1 that were not seen at t_i, which gaps turn into new alleles.
hypotheses.test: The 2005 MUSCLE alignment gives a rise of 0.053, the same within the error bars.

fields.name: rise of the other-haplotype curve over 500 bp

items.label: Discussion numbers recomputed from the paper's own rho

check.detail: 4 of 4 Discussion numbers come back from the paper's own rho = 1.4e-5: factor below template switching 21.4 (paper 20), probability of coinfection 0.0933 (paper 0.1), sweep region [bp] 155 (paper 200), distance between sweeping loci [bp] 444 (paper 400)

items.label: Discussion: factor below template switching, coinfection, sweep region, distance between sweeps

cause.summary: Three of the four numbers come back: coinfection 0.065 against 0.1, the sweep region 222 bp against 200, the distance between sweeping loci 444 bp against 400. Our rho is below the template switching rate by a factor of 31 rather than 20, which is our rho and not the arithmetic: the paper's own rho gives 21.4 (see text.arithmetic).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Our formulas differ from the paper's.
hypotheses.test: All four come back from the paper's own rho = 1.4e-05.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The gap is rho itself.
hypotheses.test: With rho = 1.4e-05 every number matches.

items.label: Methods: the allele-count cutoff at 2 or 4 gives similar results

cause.summary: The paper makes one claim about both cutoffs. At two alleles rho is 1.3e-05, within a factor of 1.4 of our 9.8e-06, but at four the fit runs into its bound (c1 = 1.0, c2 = 5.4e-06) and gives 4.1e-06, a factor of 2.4 away, so the claim does not hold on our run. The paper gives no numbers for either.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The fit needs other starting values.
The cutoff at four leaves too few pairs for this fit.
hypotheses.test: 3,570 pairs against 9,621; the outer bins hold 5 to 15 pairs.

fields.name: the cutoff at two and at four alleles gives a similar rate

cause.summary: The analysis scripts were never released. The paper says only that scripting and plotting were done in Python with NumPy and Matplotlib, and no archive, laboratory page or later repository of the group holds them.
